text:
anya (PM): quick sync — we need to lock the pricing bands + fair-usage smoothing for Q3 roadmap. customer asks piling up, and sales wants clearer burst rules.

mike_eng: +1. current tier model is too brittle for long-tail bursty workloads.

lucas_sales: a couple of enterprise customers asked for 'soft unlimited' burst for onboarding week. they expect predictable invoice behavior.

sofia_finance: soft unlimited = risky. need a smoothing policy: auto-throttle after X tokens per min but billable smoothing window over 24h.

nina_legal: flagged GDPR audit concern — any burst credits must not bypass data-residency routing. add to launch checklist.

anya (PM): proposal draft: 3 pricing bands (Starter / Scale / Enterprise) + dynamic band that allows temporary burst credits with backfill billing and a 24h smoothing window. launch criteria: docs, billing simulation, compliance sign-off, telemetry hooks.

jordan_research: metric ideas: P95 latency under burst, token cost delta before/after smoothing, # of customers hitting burst band per week.

mike_eng: implementable approach: keep hard per-second rate limits for a soft-tier-level and maintain rolling token allowance (24h). algorithm: grant N tokens/day + M burst tokens/day, burst consumed first but smoothed billing averages over window.

lucas_sales: can we express in customer-facing terms? customers hate "rolling windows" language.

sofia_finance: suggested copy: "Daily allowance + temporary burst credits; usage billed based on 24-hour average to avoid surprise spikes." simpler.

anya (PM): agree. we'll keep public wording simple, internal spec precise. also need guardrails: max burst ceiling per org to prevent abuse.

mike_eng: example config (internal):
```
rate_limit: 120 req/min
daily_allowance_tokens: 5_000_000
burst_tokens_daily: 2_000_000
smoothing_window_hours: 24
max_burst_ceiling: 10_000_000
```

jordan_research: add heuristic: if average cost over window > 150% baseline, trigger auto-notify + optional throttling.

nina_legal: ensure contract addendum for enterprise if burst_ceiling > X and include SLA exceptions.

sofia_finance: billing simulation tasks: run synthetic workloads for 5 customer personas (low, steady, onboarding-burst, seasonal, abusive). need cost delta and revenue leakage estimates.

lucas_sales: I can provide customer personas + sample traffic traces.

mike_eng: engineering tasks: implement quota engine change, expose metrics (burst_used, smoothing_billable_tokens, throttle_events), add feature flag for canary. estimated 3 sprints.

anya (PM): priority: must ship canary in Q3. OKR tie: reduce invoice surprise incidents by 60% and increase conversion from trial to paid by 8%.

devops-bot: deploy-note: canary namespace created: quota-canary-2026-q3.

jordan_research: evaluation plan: run canary for 2 weeks with 10% traffic of select orgs + synthetic stress tests. compare P50/P95 latencies and billing deltas.

sofia_finance: requirement: cost guard — if canary shows >20% unit cost increase, auto-disable burst for non-enterprise plans.

mike_eng: ack. will add circuit-breaker config.

anya (PM): launch checklist draft:
- product docs + customer-facing copy
- billing simulation results + approval
- compliance sign-off (nina)
- metrics & dashboards (we need per-org smoothing view)
- legal addendum templates for large burst ceilings
- canary plan + rollback playbook

nina_legal: I'll draft addendum language and review copy.

lucas_sales: timeline: customers expect beta in ~8 weeks. Can we meet that?

mike_eng: 3 sprints looks tight but possible if we parallelize sim + docs. dev time estimate: 6 engineer-weeks + 2 SRE-weeks for observability.

sofia_finance: I'll own billing sims, need access to logs + synthetic generator.

anya (PM): action items:
- mike_eng: spec and initial PR for quota engine this week
- sofia_finance: run billing sims and share numbers by EOW+2w
- nina_legal: draft addendum by EOW+1w
- lucas_sales: gather 3 customer personas + traces by EOW
- jordan_research: define evaluation metrics dashboard

mike_eng: starting spec now. tagging @anya for review.

lucas_sales: will loop in customer success for traces.

anya (PM): cool. next sync Thu 11am. aiming to freeze scope for Q3 planning. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: ticket created: PROD-1429 "pricing-smoothing-canary" assigned to mike_eng.

mike_eng: one more note — need to decide whether to count cached tokens vs generated tokens in smoothing calc. leaning to count generated only. thoughts?

jordan_research: counting generated only is cleaner and aligns with cost. cache hits shouldn't penalize customers.

sofia_finance: agree. billing sims should reflect that.

anya (PM): decision recorded: smoothing counts generated tokens only. documenting now.

nina_legal: minor: make sure billing language is clear on what "generated" includes.

anya (PM): will add glossary item. thanks everyone.

mike_eng: thanks — logging off to write spec.

lucas_sales: thanks team. I'll prep customer communications draft once we have numbers.

sofia_finance: added task in finance board.

end of thread.
